metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for simulation calibration and evaluation.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper states data is available from the corresponding author upon request in the Data Availability section.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts (xi, yi) coordinates from raw video frames to create position matrices mt of size X by Y.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic extraction tool not named, matrix dimensions provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Stacks N consecutive position matrices after down-sampling to represent the traffic state st.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, stacking logic and parameters fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a CNN-based Q-network using experience replay, target networks, and multitask learning to predict Q-values, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all hyperparameters and tools specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained policy in a SUMO simulation of a real-world freeway segment over 20 experiments.
tools_mentioned: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU version not stated
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulation environment and parameters fully detailed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Plots showing the convergence of episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training parameters provided, but raw traffic data and source code are not available.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel time distributions over a 1-hour simulation period for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: SUMO simulator and parameters specified; raw input traffic data not directly provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times across 20 simulation runs for three control methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed numerical results provided for multiple runs; relies on specified simulation setup.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed variations across distance and time for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualizes simulation output; depends on non-public raw traffic demand data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: On-ramp queue length distributions over time for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard simulation output; input data availability is the primary bottleneck.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot showing the relationship between signal red ratio and queue length for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation logs; methodology for red ratio calculation is specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area
nodes_sink.description: Time-series comparison of occupancy and queue length for PI-ALINEA and DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Direct visualization of simulation state variables over time.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream traffic volume at 5-minute intervals for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Aggregated simulation results; consistent with other reported metrics.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis showing travel time impact when specific spatial data subareas are perturbed.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method described, but specific data removal process lacks implementation detail.
